cards.explanation: The answer is False. Jesus asks Simon "…to put out a little from shore." (Luke 5:3). He doesn't ask for a trip across the lake. The crowd stays right there on the shore, and Jesus teaches them from the boat. A little way out, friends, and everybody can still hear.

The word is "teaches." Luke 5:3 says, "And sitting down, He taught the people from the boat." Luke 5:2 says the fishermen were washing their nets. Now Simon's boat is where the teaching happens, friends.

The answer is that they worked hard all night and caught nothing. Simon says, "we have worked hard all night without catching anything." (Luke 5:5). That's a whole night of work with nothing to show for it. I've had a rough batch or two myself, friends, and Simon's night was way bigger than that.

The answer is that Jesus says so. Simon says, "But because You say so, I will let down the nets." (Luke 5:5). After a night like that, I'd have OPINIONS about letting those nets down again. Simon gives one reason, friends, and it's what Jesus said.

The answer is False, friends! After a whole night of nothing, the nets don't come up empty. "…they caught such a large number of fish that their nets began to tear." (Luke 5:6). Nothing all night, and then nets ripping. Talk about a turnaround!

The word is "partners." Luke 5:7 says, "…they signaled to their partners in the other boat to come and help them…" The nets are tearing, so they wave over the other boat. Then both boats get filled so full that they begin to sink, friends.

The word is "sink." They "…filled both boats so full that they began to sink." (Luke 5:7). That's so many fish that two boats can barely stay up. I'd say that's the kind of problem a fisherman dreams about, friends.

The answer is that he falls at Jesus' knees. Luke 5:8 says, "When Simon Peter saw this, he fell at Jesus’ knees." The boats are so full they're beginning to sink. What Simon Peter does, friends, is drop down in front of Jesus.

The answer is that Simon Peter says, "Go away from me, Lord, for I am a sinful man" (Luke 5:8). Luke 5:9 says he and his companions were astonished at the catch of fish. I think this is a heavy moment for him, friends, and I'd just let his words stand.

The answer is True. Simon, his companions and his partners James and John are astonished at the catch, and Jesus says to Simon, "Do not be afraid…" (Luke 5:9-10). Simon had just fallen at His knees, so those words land right where he is. Short, plain and kind, friends.

The answer is catching men. Jesus says, "From now on you will catch men." (Luke 5:10). Simon is out fishing, and Jesus tells him what's ahead. The words "From now on…" tell us, friends, it's a new start.

The answer is False. Luke 5:11 says, "And when they had brought their boats ashore, they left everything and followed Him." Nobody hangs around to sell the catch, friends. They leave it all and go after Jesus.
